rounds.proof_sketch: batch_idx = blockIdx.x; grid_dims(batch_size) with batch_size=128 means blockIdx.x ∈ [0,127]. Original: (batch_idx >= 128) is false for all [0,127]. Mutated: (batch_idx > 128) is also false for all [0,127]. Both predicates always evaluate to false, so early return never triggers in either version.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the guard condition from `batch_idx >= batch_size` to `batch_idx > batch_size`. With batch_size=128 and grid dimensions set to batch_size, blockIdx.x (assigned to batch_idx) ranges from 0 to 127 inclusive. The original condition checks if batch_idx >= 128, which is never true for indices 0-127. The mutated condition checks if batch_idx > 128, which is also never true for indices 0-127. Since both conditions are always false within the valid range of block indices, both kernels execute identically for all 128 blocks, making the mutation semantically equivalent under this fixed configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant is unkillable under the fixed-shape contract because the mutated boundary check can never be reached. The grid launch configuration ensures blockIdx.x is always strictly less than batch_size (0 to 127 when batch_size=128), so neither the original (>= 128) nor mutated (> 128) conditions ever evaluate to true. Only a configuration change (which is prohibited) could expose this mutation.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing GPU kernels, boundary guards that depend on grid launch parameters should be analyzed against the actual launch configuration. If the guard protects against out-of-bounds block indices that can never be launched, mutations to such guards become semantically equivalent. Consider testing with grid oversubscription scenarios (launching more blocks than needed) to stress-test boundary guards, or use static analysis to flag guards that are provably unreachable given fixed launch parameters.
